assessment.nobel_worthiness: Biomolecular condensates reframed how cells organise their interior: liquid-liquid phase separation, a classical physical-chemical phenomenon governed by thermodynamics and multivalent interactions, is shown to build membraneless compartments. This is a new concept of molecular organisation that is general, physically grounded and has reshaped cell biology, disease research (neurodegeneration, amyloid-like transitions) and polymer physics.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne made the foundational P-granule and nucleolus demonstrations of liquid-like behaviour in cells; Rosen supplied the multivalent-interaction and in vitro reconstitution framework. Pappu and Mittag made important sequence-grammar contributions, so a three-person limit leaves real credit questions; my fair-configuration view uses Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen.
assessment.maturity: More than a decade of independent confirmation and broad adoption. The core concept is secure, though the field is still debating which cellular condensates are truly liquid and functional.
uncertainties: Debate over physiological relevance and the liquid-versus-gel nature of some condensates
Fair division among Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen, Pappu and Mittag is unresolved
Whether the work is read as chemistry or as cell biology

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are an exemplary case of lipid self-assembly and pH-dependent phase behaviour made into a delivery technology. They enabled siRNA therapeutics and mRNA vaccines, with enormous, demonstrated societal impact, resting on lipid polymorphism, pKa tuning and microfluidic mixing-controlled assembly.
assessment.attribution: The UBC group (Cullis, Hope, Madden) established the ionizable-lipid and rapid-mixing formulation principles; Anderson and Langer contributed lipidoid libraries and delivery work, and MacLachlan contributed to clinical translation. Credit is distributed across academic and industrial groups, and recognition of mRNA vaccines was already given in Medicine 2023, which complicates framing.
assessment.maturity: Clinically proven at scale, so very mature. Timing is good given the pandemic-era validation.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize may lead some to regard this as already recognised
Which of Cullis, Hope, Madden, Anderson, Langer is decisive is contested
Much of the key work is in patents and industry, making attribution harder to document

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy landscape theory with the funnel concept explained how proteins fold quickly and reliably despite a vast conformational space, using statistical mechanics and thermodynamics. It is a unifying physical-chemical principle that links theory with experiment and underpins modern understanding of folding, misfolding and aggregation, relevant to amyloid.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic (with Bryngelson and Wolynes' early work) built the landscape theory; Dill introduced the hydrophobic-collapse and lattice-model foundations; Fersht provided key experimental phi-value analysis. A three-person prize would have to leave out significant contributors.
assessment.maturity: Concepts are decades old and widely accepted. AlphaFold's 2024 prize addressed structure prediction rather than folding mechanism, so this remains an open and timely gap.
uncertainties: Competing credit between Wolynes, Onuchic, Dill and Fersht
Some committee members may view it as overshadowed by structure prediction recognition
Experimental versus theoretical emphasis is unclear

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Coordination-driven self-assembly of discrete cages and capsules established design principles for programmed molecular organisation with confined cavities, host-guest chemistry, catalysis in confined space and transport. It is an elegant case of thermodynamically controlled assembly of defined architectures.
assessment.attribution: Fujita (square and cage assemblies, encapsulation and reactivity), Raymond (tetrahedral gallium-catechol assemblies and catalysis) and Stang (directional bonding approach) are the clearest pioneers; Nitschke and Ward extended the field. Credit among the three founders is reasonably clear.
assessment.maturity: Several decades of confirmation and a broad, productive field. Applications remain largely at the research stage, and part of the territory was recognised by the 1987 and 2016 prizes (supramolecular chemistry, molecular machines).
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier supramolecular chemistry prizes
Practical impact beyond academic chemistry is still modest
Relative priority of Fujita, Raymond and Stang

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation reframes pharmacology: hijacking ubiquitin ligases to eliminate rather than inhibit proteins, with PROTACs and the mechanism of thalidomide-type molecular glues. It is conceptually new and clinically active, with compounds in late-stage trials.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies developed the PROTAC concept; Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, a decisive step for molecular glues. Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto and others have important contributions, so a three-person limit is somewhat arbitrary.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is still developing, so timing may be slightly early; the conceptual basis is already well confirmed across many groups.
uncertainties: Clinical efficacy at scale not yet established
Overlap with Ubiquitin-system prize of 2004 and potential preference for later recognition
Allocation among Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Ciulli, Gray

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalysed C-N cross-coupling made aryl amines widely accessible and is used routinely in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis. It is an important and original catalytic methodology with deep mechanistic underpinnings.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the ligand-controlled general methods; Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work is a precursor. The two-laureate configuration is clean.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature with decades of use. Palladium cross-coupling was already honoured in 2010, which could count against it.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2010 prize for Pd cross-coupling
Credit to Kosugi as precursor
Synthesis has recently been well represented relative to physical chemistry

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DNA origami demonstrated programmable, information-driven self-assembly into arbitrary nanoscale shapes, giving a general and rational route to molecular nanostructures that I find conceptually powerful from a self-assembly perspective, with uses in sensing, drug delivery and nanofabrication.
assessment.attribution: Rothemund introduced scaffolded origami; Yan and Shih extended to 3D and functional structures; Winfree and Yin made algorithmic and DNA-brick contributions. Seeman's foundational DNA nanotechnology is not on the list, which complicates the narrative of fair credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature research field with strong reproducibility, though real-world applications are still emerging.
uncertainties: Absence of foundational DNA nanotechnology credit in the supplied names
Practical impact still limited
Allocation of credit among five names is unresolved

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers produced a rapid and extraordinary rise in photovoltaic efficiency and opened a new materials class for optoelectronics. The materials chemistry, defects and ion-migration physics are interesting and widely studied.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka's original sensitised cells, Park's solid-state cells and Snaith's thin-film and planar architectures are all decisive; Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis also contributed. Credit is contested and a limited prize would be hard to assign.
assessment.maturity: Rapid progress and strong independent replication, but long-term stability and commercial status remain unsettled, so recognition may be somewhat premature.
uncertainties: Stability and toxicity limit deployment
Contested priority among Miyasaka, Park, Snaith, Grätzel, Seok
Possible premature recognition
